chapter_seo_title: Li Huowang’s New Dawn: An Unexpected Reunion in Niuxin Village
chapter_meta_description: A peaceful morning in Niuxin Village is disrupted by old tensions and new visitors—as Li Huowang reunites with a fellow survivor of the Heart-Turbid hunt.
og_title: Breakfast, Blood Scabs, and a Familiar Ghost from the Office
og_description: Neighbors argue over breakfast, Li Huowang gets scolded for scaring his wife at night, and a masked old acquaintance steps out of the morning fog.
twitter_title: Li Huowang’s peaceful morning is cut short by a familiar face in a wooden mask.
twitter_description: Domestic squabbles, free porridge, and a surprise visit from a past ally—Li Huowang can’t catch a break even in his own village.

lore_anchors.definition: The new settlement Li Huowang’s group has built after their journey; named after the nearby Niuxin Mountain, it serves as their base and a refuge for fellow survivors.
The grumpy patriarch of a small traveling opera troupe; blunt, protective, perpetually irritable toward his sons but sharp from hard-won survival.
Lü Zhuangyuan’s younger son; resentful and ambitious, he has been learning a supernatural ability and harbors intense hatred for his father.
A sycophantic survivor who ingratiated himself into Li Huowang’s group; his pregnant wife is about to deliver, and he prefers a comfortable, hands-off life over dangerous cultivation.
A fellow operative of the Supervisory Heavenly Office; the wooden-masked survivor of the same doomed mission to hunt the Heart-Turbid that killed the Chief Recorder and trapped Tuoba Danqing.
A government-sponsored supernormal law enforcement body that hunts rogue cultivators and manages supernatural disasters.
A long-standing Chinese secret religious tradition, syncretic in nature, often centered on a savior figure and the Unborn Venerable Mother; here, a recurring threat that the Office watches for.
A powerful “military path” weapon that corrupts a normal user’s personality with overwhelming bloodlust; Li Huowang remains its wielder despite its influence.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Li Huowang still covered in blood scabs at breakfast?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He practices the self-sacrificial techniques of the *Thousand Greats Record*, which demand constant self-harm and bloodletting as a source of power. Even in peace, the cost of his abilities never stops.

He is a fellow member of the Supervisory Heavenly Office who accompanied Li Huowang, the Chief Recorder, Tuoba Danqing, and the mind-blind monk on a mission to hunt a Heart-Turbid entity. Only Li Huowang and he are still “alive” and free.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Lü Xiucai hate his father so much?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Lü Xiucai resents his father’s harsh, traditional authority and his refusal to respect Xiucai’s desire to learn supernatural arts. The conflict is a classic case of a rebellious son vs. a domineering patriarch.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is this chapter important for the main plot?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It’s a character-building and world-establishing chapter. It shows the daily life of Niuxin Village, reveals simmering intragroup tensions (especially around Lü Xiucai), and introduces a returning Office agent who could later act as a witness or ally.
